body:
kelsey: Quick sync — I ran a focused sweep on microbatch sizing comparing streaming chat vs non-streaming completions. seeing p95 regressions in streaming at MB >= 8. suspect kernel fallback + KV cache churn. attaching short notes below.

mika: can you paste the numbers? p95/p99 delta and kv-hit-rate?

kelsey: sure. summary: streaming (seq len ~120): MB=4 => p95 52ms, p99 140ms, kv-hit-rate 98%. MB=8 => p95 88ms, p99 320ms, kv-hit-rate 87%. MB=12 => p95 140ms, p99 610ms, kv-hit-rate 69%

samir: ouch. that looks like tail blowup not linear throughput. did you see kernel fallback logs (slow-kernel) during those MB spikes?

kelsey: yes — stack traces show fallback to fallback_attention_kernel at several tails. profiling shows those requests hit a codepath that disables certain fused kernels when kv-span > 64k.

jordan: kv-span threshold? is that in bytes or tokens?

kelsey: tokens. when total cached KV tokens for batch > 4096 we see kernel chooser prefer a generic kernel to avoid OOM on some GPUs. that generic kernel is ~3-5x slower for those long prefixes.

mika: that explains the p99. streaming accumulates KV across turns so you get uneven per-request kv-loads. completions reset per request, so less spill. what about microbatch composition — are streaming MBs more heterogeneous?

kelsey: yes. streaming batches had high variance: many small interactive requests + occasional long-turn follow-ups. the long ones push the kernel chooser into fallback. completions workload was uniform (single-shot), so it hit fast kernels consistently.

samir: two levers: 1) adjust batching heuristic to cap effective MB for streaming when kv-span variance high, 2) change kernel selection policy to bias fast fused kernels even if kv-span slightly > threshold (risky).

jordan: can we also pre-split batches by estimated kv-span? e.g., compute rough prefix token estimate and keep high-span requests in separate microbatches. cheap classifier before enqueue.

kelsey: tried a heuristic: tag reqs with est_kv_tokens then do two pools: low and high. results: allowing MB up to 12 in low pool kept p95 ~60ms; high pool enforced MB<=2 and p95 ~95ms but p99 reduced from 610ms to 210ms. overall throughput dropped ~6% but tail much better.

perf-bot: profiling artifact uploaded: https://internal.redwood/profiles/2100001234/summary — contains flamegraphs for MB=4/8/12 + kernel chooser traces.

mika: nice. can we tune the KV cache policy too? maybe trim rarely-used KV entries for streaming to keep kv-span smaller for long sessions.

samir: trimming is possible but may hurt quality for very long convs. another option: adaptive quantization on cached KV to reduce memory footprint and keep fused kernels enabled. that requires kernel support.

ops: note — Dedicated customers may see different behavior due to GPU memory profiles; please simulate on a1/gpu-large before rolling.

kelsey: agreed. plan propose: (A) rollout batching heuristic change (pre-split by est_kv_tokens) to canary 10% for streaming routes, MB caps: low pool 12, high pool 2; (B) add logging for kernel-fallback reasons (kv-span vs mem), (C) perf team to prototype lightweight kv-trim policy and measure quality regression.

mika: +1. what about an immediate mitigation for hosted API — default streaming MB cap to 6 for prod until we validate?

samir: safe. also add a p99 alert that triggers on >2x baseline for a route.

kelsey: I'll open a PR with the batching changes and config flags. PR will include a small experiment harness and rollout playbook.

jordan: cc @ops for canary infra. ops: can we schedule canary later today?

ops: yes, we have a free slot at 18:00 UTC. will reserve a dedicated pool and monitor GPU mem/OOM logs.

kelsey: thanks — will post PR link and a short experiment runbook. action items: kelsey PR, samir prototype kv-trim, perf-bot provide full flamegraphs.

mika: thanks all. short follow-up: add a note to docs about streaming vs single-shot MB defaults. :thumbsup:
